verdict: Eversource's revenue fell 7.5% to $2.98 billion and earnings slipped to $346 million, or $0.92 a share, as regulators cut its allowed transmission return and disallowed Connecticut storm costs.

segments.name: Energy delivery revenue
segments.note: Everything Eversource collected for delivering electricity and natural gas across Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire. Eversource reports one combined revenue line and breaks out earnings — not revenue — by segment.

opex.name: Operations & maintenance
opex.note: Crews, repairs and running the grid and gas network day to day.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization, net
opex.note: Depreciation of $382M on poles, wires and pipes, minus a $120M regulatory amortization credit.

opex.name: Energy efficiency programs
opex.note: Regulator-approved programs that help customers use less energy; the cost is recovered in rates.

opex.name: Taxes other than income taxes
opex.note: Mainly property taxes on the network.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $349M, partly offset by $117M of other income (largely the allowance for funds used during construction and pension-related credits) — a net $232M cost. There were no offshore-wind losses this quarter.

takeaways.title: A reset quarter
takeaways.text: GAAP and recurring EPS were both $0.92 with no adjustments this quarter — versus $1.19 of recurring EPS a year ago, before the FERC return cut and the storm-cost disallowance.

takeaways.title: Transmission is the anchor
takeaways.text: Electric transmission earned $182M and electric distribution $201M, while natural gas lost $43M in its seasonally weak quarter after a Massachusetts rate-design change shifted revenue between quarters.

takeaways.title: Guidance midpoint raised
takeaways.text: Management narrowed 2026 recurring EPS guidance to $4.62–$4.70 and lifted the midpoint to $4.66, keeping the 5–7% long-term growth target through 2030.

oneTimers: Year-to-date (not this quarter) GAAP results carry three large charges: $111M after tax on the Aquarion water sale, $164M for higher expected offshore-wind exit payments, and $44M for refunds after FERC cut the New England transmission return on equity from 10.57% to 9.57%.
Connecticut regulators (PURA) disallowed part of CL&P's previously deferred storm costs in a July 29, 2026 decision, which weighed on electric distribution earnings this quarter.
footerNote: Eversource reports a single combined operating-revenue line, so this chart shows one revenue segment; segment earnings are covered in the takeaways. Net income of $348M is the consolidated total; $346M was attributable to common shareholders. Figures are from the official release's condensed consolidated statements, reported in $ thousands and rounded here to the nearest $M.
